name: Belgium
headline: Belgium: +1.0% growth in 2025, 3.0% inflation, debt 108% of GDP
sections: Belgium is a $725 billion economy (2025), the world's 23rd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.0% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $75K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 11.2% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 3.0% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 10.3% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 6.2% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 17.8% (2025).
Gross government debt is 108% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has fallen from 111% in 2020. The general government balance is −5.2% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −1.9% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 153% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were −4.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 122% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 82.3 years (2024). Population: 11.9 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
